Looping in Ethan (SE) and Dev (platform engineer) to answer the technical bits — see initial integration notes below. Also attached: integration_checklist.xlsx and redwood_sdk_quickstart.md.

Quick answers:
- Streaming: Yes — Redwood supports streaming token-by-token over an HTTP/2 streaming endpoint (POST /v1/streams). We also support chunked server-sent events for browser clients. Typical pattern: open stream, send initial prompt + config, receive incremental tokens + structured event for tool calls.
- Tool/Function calling: Supported. Redwood returns structured JSON events when a model requests a tool; you can implement a tool handler that calls your external systems and send function results back to the model via the same stream or a follow-up request. See the SDK sample route /v1/functions/call in the quickstart.
- SDKs: We have official JS & Python SDKs; quickstart shows the minimal call and streaming example. Link: https://docs.redwood.ai/sdk (also attached quickstart md).
- Auth: Use a service account key with scoped permissions (read-only for embeddings/beta features if needed). We recommend rotating keys every 90 days. We'll provide a template IAM policy.

Integration checklist highlights (from attached):
1) Create service account + key in staging.
2) Whitelist staging IPs (if you prefer network allowlist).
3) Implement basic generate flow (POST /v1/generate) then upgrade to streaming for latency-sensitive flows.
4) Add prefix caching for repeated prompts; Redwood supports KV prefix caching to cut down on tokens.
5) Instrument token-level logging and sample storage for quality evals (we can set retention per contract).

Attachments: integration_checklist.xlsx, redwood_sdk_quickstart.md

Ethan/Dev — can you confirm estimated engineering effort for a standard integration (approx hours) and whether we should provide a small starter repo for Acme?
